resale_co.name: Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (Resale C.O. for an existing structure)
resale_co.issued_by: Building Department (Office of Inspection); housing inspection by the housing official
requirements: Notarized Heat Certification from the seller or agent that the heating system, water heater and any fireplace or wood/solid-fuel stove were inspected by a professional

Stafford Municipal Utility Authority letter confirming water and sewer service (if on S.M.U.A.); private wells tested by a licensed well driller or tester and approved by the Ocean County Health Department
Lot and exterior in good condition (roofing, siding, no chipped or badly weathered paint)
House numbers on the structure, 3 inches for residential
Chimney caps on all fireplace chimneys

Electrical: no exposed connections or missing plates, secure fixtures with globes on exterior and closet lights, no open spaces in the panel, no extension cords as permanent wiring, ceiling fans permanently wired, service equipment properly supported

Plumbing and heating: proper venting of heating equipment; water heater and boiler relief valves piped down to within 6 inches of the floor; cold on the right and hot on the left; no leaks; metal dryer vents

Smoke detectors within 10 feet of any sleeping area and at least one on each level including the basement; 10-year sealed battery alarms where battery alarms are used; hardwired alarms may not be replaced with battery alarms
CO detectors within 10 feet of sleeping areas in homes with fuel-burning appliances or an attached garage
Bathroom exhaust fans working if installed
Porches, decks and stairs secure; handrails on stairs with more than 3 risers; guardrails on open sides 30 inches or more above grade
Interior in satisfactory condition with holes repaired and painted
resale_co.how_to_apply: Fill out the Application for Existing Structure Certificate of Occupancy (check 'Resale C.O.', and in Special Instructions say how the inspector gets in: key, lock box number, owner home). Include the notarized Heat Certification form (clerical staff can notarize it at the counter) and the S.M.U.A. water/sewer letter or approved well test. Submit to Building Inspections, 260 East Bay Avenue, Manahawkin, 609-597-1000 ext 8532.

evidence.quote: Issue Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (rental/resale property)
public swimming pools; housing inspection for resale and rental properties.

The “Heat Certification” form (PDF) is also needed before a C.C.O. can be issued. This is a notarized statement by the seller, or his agent, verifying the condition of the heating systems and fireplaces (free-standing stoves, wood burning stoves or any solid fuel burners) were inspected by a professional.
Inspection by the housing official consists of a visual review only. It is not a thorough, in depth structural investigation of the dwelling.
APPLICATION FOR EXISTING STRUCTURE CERTIFICATE OF OCCUPANCY
Building Inspections Physical Address 260 East Bay Avenue Manahawkin, NJ 08050 609-597-1000 ext 8532 Edmond Alvare Construction Official / Zoning Official 609-597-1000 ext 8563

resale_co.notes: The Building Department page lists 'housing inspection for resale and rental properties' and 'Issue Continuing Certificate of Occupancy (rental/resale property)' among its duties, and its Rentals & Resales page gives the application (Resale C.O. $40.00 on the 2023 form), the seller's Heat Certification and the list of common violations. The Rentals & Resales page cites Stafford Code Chapter 81 for rentals (inspection at every change of occupancy, at most once a year). The construction permit fee schedule (revised 05/15/18) separately lists 'CERTIFICATE OF CONTINUED OCCUPANCY $150.00'; that is the construction-code certificate, not the resale housing C.O. shown on the resale application. The application has lines for a first, second and third inspection but no re-inspection fee amount. The Building Department does not list an email address; general office line 609-597-1000 ext 8532 (Principal Clerk Typist Kristin Unley). Rentals only: seasonal rental C.O. $100, and pre-1978 long-term rentals need lead-based paint inspections.

requirements: Smoke alarms on every living level including the basement; on bedroom levels within 10 feet of the bedroom door
Ceiling mounting preferred; wall alarms 4 to 12 inches below the ceiling, 4 inches from corners and at least 3 feet from air registers
All smoke alarms, including hardwired ones, under 10 years old

By year built: before 1978 at least one 10-year sealed battery alarm per level; 1978 to 1983 hardwired alarms on each level; 1984 to 1990 interconnected hardwired alarms with battery backup on each level; 1991 to present interconnected hardwired alarms with battery backup in bedrooms and on each level
Hardwired detectors cannot be replaced with battery detectors

CO alarms in the immediate vicinity of sleeping areas in homes with a fuel-burning device or attached garage; battery-only and plug-in CO alarms under 5 years old; combination smoke/CO alarms under 10 years old

Homes with a generator, solar panels, battery storage or other secondary power source need a printed ANSI Z535.4 label (wording like 'CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER') within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and the electric meter
No fire extinguisher item on the current Stafford requirements sheet

authorities.name: Stafford Township Bureau of Fire Prevention (Fire Official)
authorities.lead_time: 10 or more business days before closing for the lowest fee; inspections Tuesdays and Thursdays 9 am to 1 pm

fees.label: 10 or more business days notice before closing
4 business days or less before closing

authorities.how_to_apply: Send the completed Application for Smoke / CO Detector Certification (with the closing date) to FIRE@STAFFORDNJ.GOV or drop it off at the Fire Prevention Office, 260 East Bay Ave, Manahawkin. Payment must be dropped off at the Fire Prevention Office by check or cash only; scheduling is done after payment, in person or by phone. Inspections are Tuesdays and Thursdays 9 am to 1 pm. Certificates for passed inspections are picked up at the Fire Prevention Office the next business day.

fire_cert.notes: Fees are from the Township's current smoke/CO application (the Fire Prevention page says 'FEES ARE LISTED ON APPLICATION'); the posted 'Smoke Detector Inspection Ordinance' (Section 111-6A, Chapter 111 Fire Prevention) shows the same $45 / $90 / $161 schedule plus $25 re-inspections, but the posted copy has a blank ordinance number and blank 2026 meeting dates, so its adoption date is not confirmed. The application and requirements sheet are scanned images, so quotes were read from the page images. Other fire staff: Fire Inspectors Alyssa Chapman (AChapman@staffordnj.gov, (609) 597-1000 x8527) and Michael Donahue (MDonahue@staffordnj.gov, (609) 597-1000 x8617). The state directory (Stafford is code 1530 there) lists the same Fire Official. Seasonal rental ($125) and commercial ($125) fees are not resale fees.

other_items.label: Heat certification
other_items.detail: Notarized statement by the seller or agent that the heating system, water heater and any fireplace or wood/solid-fuel stove were inspected by a professional; needed before the C.C.O. is issued. Staff can notarize it at the counter.

other_items.label: Water and sewer / well
other_items.detail: Provide a Stafford Municipal Utility Authority letter confirming water and sewer are supplied by the S.M.U.A.; existing well water must be tested by a licensed well driller or tester and approved by the Ocean County Health Department (732 341-9700).
